title: Dynamic Threat Matrix: Early-warning Signals for Micro-model Entrants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an operationalized early-warning system and playbook that surfaces micro-model entrants and capability shifts likely to displace Redwood's short-context or latency-sensitive product buckets. Deliverables: a threat matrix taxonomy, signal prioritizer, recon runbook for field probes, and a lightweight dashboard spec for continuous monitoring.
background: Recent field probes and customer escalations indicate small, specialized open models (micro-models) are iterating quickly on narrow capabilities and deployment patterns that can undercut our latency-sensitive offerings. Existing model-watch artifacts focus on big entrants; we lack an operational pattern for low-cost micro entrants that can rapidly erode P2/P1 customer segments.
goals: Define taxonomy of micro-model threat vectors (latency arbitrage, quantization-optimized variants, region-latency-footprint)
Produce signal scoring rubric to prioritize field probes and remediation work
Ship a reconnaissance runbook for Solutions and Growth to validate customer-impact hypotheses within 2 weeks
Deliver dashboard spec with 4 KPIs to track threat velocity and coverage
success_metrics: Median detection lead time <= 14 days from initial public mention to internal alert
At least 80% of high-priority signals validated or invalidated via field probes within a 10-day window
Reduction in surprise escalations for latency-sensitive customers by 30% quarter-over-quarter
scope_includes: Signal taxonomy and prioritizer for public+private signals (GitHub releases, model zoo updates, benchmark chatter, cloud marketplace listings)
Runbook for 3 rapid field probe types: automated microbench, customer telemetry check, targeted outreach
Dashboard wireframe and API contract for ingesting scored signals
scope_excludes: Full ingestion pipeline implementation (this ticket defines APIs/spec only)
Broad model cataloging unrelated to latency/short-context threats
approach: Phase 1: Research & taxonomy sprint (2 weeks) — mine public repos, community forums, marketplace changelogs, and internal support logs for candidate signals. Phase 2: Scoring rubric and runbook design (1 week) — synthesize signal weightings and probe playbooks. Phase 3: Dashboard spec + handoff (1 week). Use lean artifacts: Google Sheet signal register, Confluence PRD stub, Figma wireframe. Coordinate with Research for microbench code snippets and with Solutions for probe execution.

risks: High false-positive rate if signals are naively scraped from social chatter
Overloading Solutions with probes — need prioritization guardrails
Engineering bandwidth for dashboard spec adoption may slip into next cycle
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decided to prioritize precision over recall for initial phase to avoid wasted probe effort. Tradeoff: may miss slow-burn threats. Chosen signal sources: GitHub releases, model hub tags, cloud marketplace 'new' flags, and public benchmark posts. Deferred scraping chat forums until initial precision tests complete.
